generic.authority: the registration office of your country
generic.association: the beekeepers' association of your country
generic.plant: the processing plant of your country
generic.phone: a test number of your country (see Table "Demo accounts")
generic.region: the region of your country, e.g. Entre Ríos (AR)

labels.ccp0Values: **CCP 0 (primary audit):** answer every yes/no question with **Yes**. Text questions: "If yes, which methods…": {if}; "To what extent…": {extent}; the other text question: {text}.

roles.name: Platform administrator
roles.who: The team that runs the platform for the project (in real life: the platform operator).
does: verifies organizations and gives them their capabilities
adds members and sends them their sign-in details
creates batches from the approved lots of a plant (for now only administrators do this)
decides delivery corrections together with a second administrator
reads every record, the audit log and the recall report, but never enters business data
roles.screens: Dashboard, Organizations, Beekeepers, Wholesalers → Final Honey Productions, User Management (audit log, notices, data retention)

roles.name: Beekeeper registration officer
roles.who: An officer of the authority that keeps the register of beekeepers ({{org.authority}}).
does: checks the beekeeper's registry number and identity
records the beekeeper and the first apiary
lets the beekeeper read the information notice and records the consents
confirms the registration with the code the beekeeper receives by SMS, or with a signed form
sends the beekeeper the sign-in details for the beekeeper portal

roles.name: Organization admin
roles.who: The manager of an organization in the platform: here of the beekeepers' association ({{org.association}}) and of the plant ({{org.plant}}).
does: keeps the organization's documents and data-controller details up to date
association: records a beekeeper's consent for a public beekeeper page
plant: reads the deliveries, the samples and the beekeepers' asking prices
can request finalizing and ship, like Staff
roles.screens: My organization (organization page, documents), Beekeeper pages (association), Shipments and stock (plant)

roles.name: Field inspector
roles.who: A technician of the beekeepers' association ({{org.association}}).
does: reads the lots, batches and lab reports of the association's members
enters CCP 0 (the primary audit at the beekeeper) only if an administrator gives CCP 0 to the association; by default the plant does it
roles.screens: My work, My organization, recall report

roles.name: Sample acceptance officer
roles.who: The person at the reception of the processing plant ({{org.plant}}).
does: records each delivery container by container, with weights and seals
fills a sample jar and a counter-sample jar from every container, with tamper-evident caps
lets the beekeeper confirm the delivery with the SMS code
prints the labels and sends the jars to the laboratory
enters CCP 0 (primary audit) of every new lot
roles.screens: Deliveries (intake) → Record a delivery, the delivery page with Labels, Samples and lab, My work → Values to enter

roles.name: Staff
roles.who: A production worker of the plant ({{org.plant}}).
does: enters the CCP values of the lots (CCP 2–3) and of the batches (CCP 4–10)
requests finalizing of a batch when everything is complete
ships a finalized batch to a customer
roles.screens: My work → Values to enter, My organization → batch, Shipments and stock → Ship

roles.name: Quality Assurance Officer
roles.who: The second person who checks the work of others: at the plant ({{org.plant}}) and at the shop ({{org.shop}}).
does: approves the CCP records that another person entered (four-eyes principle)
confirms finalizing: the batch is sealed and its Honey Story goes public
at the shop: approves the storage record (CCP 10)
roles.screens: My work → Values to approve, Finalize requests; Shipments and stock → Storage

roles.name: Analyst
does: receives every sample jar and checks the seal number, the label and the tamper-evident cap
makes the composite sample of a lot
enters the lab results, uploads the report PDF and submits the report
roles.screens: My work → Samples to receive, Lab results to enter; Samples and lab

roles.name: Lab manager
does: approves or returns the reports the analysts submit (never their own results)
approval writes the results into the lot's CCP 1
roles.screens: My work → Lab reports to approve; the public page Verify a lab report

roles.name: Compliance Officer
roles.who: The person who supervises how an organization works with the platform. In the demo one account has this role in every organization of the country; switch between them with the organization chip at the top.
does: accepts or rejects signed photos that replace an SMS code
reviews the sampling quality: rejected jars, broken seals, deliveries confirmed by photo
watches the approval mechanism and the audit entries of the organization
records data-subject requests and keeps the data-controller details
roles.screens: Compliance, My work → Review signed photos

roles.name: Shop (retailer)
roles.who: The staff of a shop that receives honey ({{org.shop}}).
does: confirms or rejects the receipt of a shipment
records the storage conditions (CCP 10), which its Quality Assurance Officer approves
reads the producer's records of the batch, read-only
roles.screens: My work → Shipments to confirm; Shipments and stock → Storage

roles.name: Beekeeper (portal)
roles.who: The beekeeper, with their own small part of the platform (the beekeeper portal).
does: follows their deliveries, containers, seals and sample jars
sees approved lab results, the batches with their honey and their Honey Story pages
enters an asking price per kg for each delivery (until the batch is finalized)
gives or withdraws their consents
roles.screens: My beekeeper area: Home, My deliveries, Samples and lab, Batches with my honey, My Honey Story pages, Privacy and consents

roles.name: Consumer (public)
roles.who: Anyone who scans the QR code on a jar. No account.
does: reads the Honey Story: where the honey comes from, the lab results with their limits, the control points
opens the beekeeper's page when the beekeeper agreed
checks a lab report on the page Verify a lab report
roles.screens: Honey Story (QR code), beekeeper page, Verify a lab report

steps.title: Register a beekeeper
do: Open **Beekeeper registration**, type a registry number such as {{registry}} (nn: two digits of your choice) and click **Find or register**.
Fill in the beekeeper: first name **[DEMO] and your first name**, a last name, the birth date, the mobile phone {{phone}} (nn: two digits of your choice) and the language of the SMS.
Apiary: click the map or type the coordinates, choose **Province** {{region}}, a district (e.g. {{district}}), type the locality and the number of hives.

Read the notice with the "beekeeper". Tick **The beekeeper agrees that their name is shown on public pages** (then the name appears in the Honey Story), the attestation and **Also send the beekeeper the sign-in details by SMS**.
Click **Send code**. Open **Demo SMS inbox** (link at the bottom of the page, it opens in a new tab), copy the 6-digit code, enter it and click **Confirm the registration**.
steps.expect: "The beekeeper is registered and verified; the sign-in details were sent by SMS." The page shows the beekeeper with a business number such as {{bn}}. Write it down: the plant needs it.

steps.title: Give the sign-in details to the beekeeper
do: Open **Demo SMS inbox** again. The newest message is the beekeeper's sign-in SMS: user name (the business number) and a temporary password.
Give both to the tester who plays the beekeeper (step B2).
steps.expect: The SMS shows the user name and a 10-character temporary password, valid for 72 hours. On the live site this SMS reaches only the beekeeper's phone.

steps.title: Record the delivery with sealed containers
do: Open **Deliveries (intake)** → **Record a delivery**, type the business number from step A1 and click **Find**.
Choose the apiary, the honey type, the production period ([DEMO] Test season 2026–2027), the delivery date, **Country of origin** {{countryName}}, **Province** {{region}} and the district.
Choose the laboratory **{{org.lab}}**. The list holds the laboratories of every partner country: take your own.

Containers: one row per container (**Add a container** for the second). Enter the net kg and the seals: the seal on arrival (or a plant seal), the jar seal, the counter-sample seal, the new seal after sampling. Use seal numbers with your initials, every number different. Tick **Cap intact** for each jar.
Click **Send code**, read the code in **Demo SMS inbox** (the beekeeper's SMS lists the containers and weights), enter it and click **Confirm the delivery**.
steps.expect: "Delivery confirmed by the beekeeper and recorded as lot #…". The delivery page shows the containers and their seal history; **Labels** prints the labels with QR codes (optional).

steps.title: The beekeeper signs in and sets the asking price
do: Sign in with the business number and the temporary password from step A2, and choose your own password (at least 10 characters). Read and confirm the notice.
Open **My deliveries**, enter an asking price per kg in {{currency}} for the new delivery and click **Enter price**.
steps.expect: "Price saved." The price can change until the batch is finalized (step D5); then it is locked. Only the plant, its Compliance Officer and the platform administrators see it.

steps.title: CCP 0: the primary audit
do: Open **My work** → **Values to enter** → **CCP 0** of the new lot.
Answer every question (suggested answers in Table "Suggested values") and click **Save Monitoring Logs**.
steps.expect: "… values saved." The status becomes **Submitted**; the task moves to the Quality Assurance Officer.

steps.title: Approve CCP 0
do: Open **My work** → **Values to approve** → CCP 0 of the lot, check the answers and click **Approve**.
steps.expect: "CCP record approved." Only now can the laboratory enter results for this lot.

steps.title: Receive the sample jars
do: Open **My work** → **Samples to receive** (or **Samples and lab**). For each jar of the lot answer the three checks (the seal number matches the record, the label is intact, the cap is intact) with **Yes** and click **Record the reception**.
When every container's jar is received, click **Make the composite**.

Optional: answer **No** for the cap of one jar. The jar is rejected; the plant takes a new jar from the same container (delivery page → **Open, sample and seal again**), and the Compliance Officer sees the rejection (step F1).
steps.expect: "Jar received" for each jar; the composite sample S-…-COMP opens with the lab report form.

steps.title: Enter the lab results
do: On the composite's report: enter a report number, the date of issue and every value (suggested values in Table "Suggested values"; try one value outside its limit if you like).
Upload a PDF as the report (you can use demo-lab-report.pdf from this pack), click **Save**, then **Submit for approval**.
steps.expect: "Report submitted; a Lab manager (another person) must approve it." The counter of required values shows that all are entered.

steps.title: Approve the lab report
do: Open **My work** → **Lab reports to approve**, open the report, check it and click **Approve** (values outside their limits ask for a confirmation).
steps.expect: "Lab report approved; the results are now the lot's CCP 1 values." The report can now be checked on the public page **Verify a lab report**.

steps.title: CCP 2 and CCP 3 of the lot
do: Staff: **My work** → **Values to enter** → CCP 2, enter the values, **Save Monitoring Logs**; the same for CCP 3.
Quality Assurance Officer ({{u.quality}}): **My work** → **Values to approve** → **Approve** each.
steps.expect: Both records **Completed** with an approval. The lot is now complete and can go into a batch.

steps.title: Create the batch
do: Open **Wholesalers** → {{org.plant}} → **Final Honey Productions** → **New Batch**. Enter a title with your initials (e.g. [DEMO] Batch AB) and the production date, click **Create Batch**.
On **Manage Batch** enter the amount (kg) to use from your lot and click **Save Batch Composition**.
Open **Manage CCP**, switch CCP 4 to CCP 10 to **Yes** and click **Save Assignments**.
**Edit** the batch and choose the owning organization {{org.plant}}.
steps.expect: The batch lists your lot and CCP 4–10. Creating batches is an administrator's task for now.

steps.title: CCP 4 to CCP 10 of the batch
do: Staff: **My work** → **Values to enter**: enter the values of CCP 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 of the batch and click **Save Monitoring Logs** on each.
Quality Assurance Officer ({{u.quality}}): approve each one.
steps.expect: Seven records **Completed**. CCP 10 here is the storage at the plant.

steps.title: Request finalizing
do: Open **My organization** → your batch → **Request finalizing**. If the button is disabled, the page lists what is still missing.
steps.expect: "Finalizing requested; a Quality Assurance Officer (another person) must confirm it."

steps.title: Finalize: the batch is sealed
do: Open **My work** → **Finalize requests** → the batch → **Confirm and finalize**.
steps.expect: "Batch finalized." The batch page shows the seal and the link to the public Honey Story with its QR code. The batch, its lots and the beekeeper's price are now locked.

steps.title: Ship the batch to the shop
do: Open **Shipments and stock** → **Ship** next to your batch, choose {{org.shop}}, enter a quantity in kg and click **Ship**.
steps.expect: "Shipment created; custody moves when the receiver confirms it."

steps.title: The shop confirms the receipt
do: Open **My work** → **Shipments to confirm** (or **Shipments and stock**) and click **Confirm receipt** (or **Reject** with a reason).
steps.expect: "Receipt confirmed; you now hold this quantity."

steps.title: Storage at the shop (CCP 10)
do: Open **Shipments and stock** → **Storage** next to the batch, enter the temperature and the relative humidity and click **Save**.
The shop's Quality Assurance Officer ({{u.shopquality}}) opens the same page and approves.
steps.expect: "Storage values saved.", then "CCP record approved." The shop can also read the producer's records of the batch, read-only.

steps.title: The Compliance Officer reviews
do: With the organization chip at the top, switch to **{{org.plant}}**. Open **Compliance** → **Sampling quality**, click **Write a review** next to a rejected jar, choose **in order** or **finding**, write what you checked and save.

Switch to **{{org.authority}}**. Open **My work** → **Review signed photos**: the registration of {{b3.name}} waits with a signed form. Open it and click **Accept** (if another tester already did, it shows the decision).
Look at **Approval mechanism** and **Audit entries** on the Compliance page.
steps.expect: "Review recorded." and "Evidence accepted; the registry number is verified." A person never reviews an item they recorded themselves.

steps.title: The beekeeper sees the result
do: Sign in as the beekeeper of step B2. Open **Batches with my honey** and **My Honey Story pages**.
steps.expect: The finalized batch with the beekeeper's share and the link to its Honey Story. Other beekeepers' names and prices are never shown.

steps.title: The consumer opens the Honey Story
do: Scan the QR code of the batch (batch page or label) with a phone, or open the Honey Story link of the batch page.
Also open the example honey of your country: {{example.story}}
steps.expect: The Honey Story: the beekeeper's name (with consent), the origin {{countryName}}, the approved lab results with their limits and the control points. The province map shows Türkiye only (see "Limits of the demo").

questions: Could you follow one honey from the beekeeper to the shop shelf? (1 = not at all, 5 = easily)
Which step was the hardest, and why?
Which labels, messages or texts were unclear in your language?
What does not match the practice in your country (registration, delivery, sampling, laboratory, labelling, shops)?
Which data would your country need that the platform does not record?
Did you use a phone or a tablet? Which device and browser, and did it work?
Would beekeepers in your country use the beekeeper portal (asking price, consents)? What would they need?
Anything else you want to tell us?
